Pulsar added USDT deposits through TRON's TRC-20 network on November 19.

Supported stablecoin deposits carry no Pulsar fees, but network and third-party charges may apply.

TRON reported $2.21 trillion in Q3 stablecoin settlement volume, not Pulsar-specific activity.

Pulsar USDT deposits are giving users another route to spend stablecoins without first converting them through a traditional bank transfer. The November 19 integration supports USDT on TRON, letting eligible users fund their accounts and pay through Pulsar’s virtual card.

It’s a practical addition. But don’t confuse a new deposit option with proof of a sudden stablecoin spending boom.

Users can deposit USDT through the TRON network and use supported balances for online purchases, subscriptions and other everyday expenses.

The process requires selecting USDT and the TRON (TRC-20) network in the Pulsar app, then sending funds to the deposit address provided for that network.

Pulsar says supported stablecoin deposits carry no fees across its plans. However, network and third-party charges may still apply. Availability can also vary by region and service provider.

The launch comes as TRON reports substantial stablecoin activity. Its Q3 2026 settlement volume reached $2.21 trillion, averaging approximately $24 billion daily, according to the announcement.

TRON DAO also reported more than $94 billion in circulating USDT on the network.

Those figures show the scale of the underlying ecosystem, not Pulsar’s adoption. The announcement disclosed no user numbers, deposit totals or completed card-payment volumes.

For now, Pulsar USDT deposits expand access to stablecoin-funded payments. Whether users actually spend more through the virtual card remains an unanswered question.

Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth."

Paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

About $2.8 billion worth of RLUSD is in circulation, compared with about $180 billion worth of Tether's USDT. Tether's stablecoin is still more than 60 times bigger than RLUSD.

Ripple launched RLUSD in December 2024. In mid-September 2026, RLUSD supply passed $2.44 billion, and about $1.38 billion of it was on Ethereum. About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he said.

The ETF industry is entering a new phase of competition. Once dominated by low-cost index funds, the market is expanding into active management, cryptocurrency exposure, derivatives-based strategies and specialized investment themes. The shift is changing how asset managers develop products and compete for investor capital. Global ETF assets reached $22.83 trillion in September 2026, while U.S.-listed funds attracted another $204.2 billion in October. Yet the more important change is happening in capital allocation: investors are increasingly using ETFs to access strategies that extend well beyond traditional market indexes.

This report examines the key trends reshaping the ETF market, the rise of new investment products, and how these developments could redefine asset management.

The global ETF market added more than $4 trillion in assets during the first nine months of 2026, supported by investor inflows and gains across financial markets. According to data, global ETF assets increased from $18.69 trillion at the end of 2025 to $22.83 trillion by September 30, 2026. Net inflows contributed $2.25 trillion, while market appreciation added another $1.89 trillion.

More significantly, nine-month inflows had already exceeded the previous full-year record of $2.09 trillion set in 2025. Equity ETFs remained the industry’s largest segment, with $17.74 trillion in assets, followed by bond ETFs at $3.57 trillion. Alternative ETFs held $772.1 billion, while commodity ETFs accounted for $471.7 billion.

Active management is emerging as one of the ETF industry’s fastest-growing segments. The appeal is straightforward: investors can access portfolio managers’ security selection and allocation decisions through an exchange-traded structure. The latest inflow figures suggest that demand is expanding faster than the segment’s existing asset share.

Active ETFs attracted $675.2 billion in net inflows during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $1.58 trillion for passive products. That gave active funds nearly 30% of total ETF inflows, despite representing just 12.81% of industry assets.

The gap between asset share and inflow share is significant. Active ETFs are attracting a larger proportion of new money than their current market presence would suggest. Product launches reinforce that shift. Of the 89 U.S. ETFs launched in October, 65% were actively managed, according to FactSet. Equity strategies accounted for approximately half of new launches.

Cryptocurrency ETFs have created a new distribution channel between digital assets and traditional financial markets. Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum products allow investors to gain exposure through conventional brokerage accounts rather than directly managing wallets, private keys or exchange accounts. This has made digital assets more accessible to investors who prefer established investment platforms and fund structures.

The development also brings traditional asset managers into direct competition for crypto allocations. Firms such as BlackRock and Fidelity can distribute digital asset products through established investment networks, while specialist providers compete through product design, fees and market positioning.

Crypto ETFs remain exposed to price volatility, custody arrangements, liquidity conditions and regulatory uncertainty. The wider significance is that digital assets are becoming part of the ETF product landscape rather than remaining confined to dedicated cryptocurrency exchanges.

Options-based ETFs are expanding the range of outcomes investors can pursue through exchange-traded products. Covered-call funds, buffer ETFs and defined-outcome strategies are increasingly being used to target income, manage downside exposure or modify participation in market gains.

The growth of ETF-linked derivatives trading provides a measure of the activity surrounding these products. Cboe reported that ETF options averaged 28.3 million contracts per day in the third quarter of 2026, up 1% from the previous quarter. Single-stock options averaged 32.7 million contracts, while index options recorded 6.1 million.

The activity highlights ETFs’ growing role in the derivatives market. It also provides an important foundation for products built around option premiums and defined investment outcomes.

Asset managers are increasingly using thematic ETFs to package exposure to industries expected to benefit from long-term economic and technological changes.

Artificial intelligence, semiconductor manufacturing, cybersecurity, defense, nuclear energy and critical minerals are among the themes attracting investment interest. These products allow investors to access groups of companies linked to a particular industry without selecting individual stocks.

The scale of the broader U.S. ETF market illustrates the opportunity. U.S. ETF assets increased from $12.63 trillion in September 2025 to $16.15 trillion in September 2026, while the number of funds expanded from 4,181 to 5,368, according to the Investment Company Institute.

The ETF expansion is not being driven exclusively by new investment products. Traditional asset managers are also reconsidering how existing strategies are packaged and distributed.

Mutual fund-to-ETF conversions offer a route to bring established portfolios into an exchange-traded structure. For eligible U.S. funds, the structure can provide potential tax advantages, intraday trading and access to brokerage distribution networks. The shift is particularly relevant for active managers. Instead of building a new strategy from the ground up, firms can consider offering existing investment approaches through ETFs.

October’s launch activity illustrates the direction of product development: 65% of the 89 new U.S. ETFs launched that month were actively managed. FactSet also reported that equity strategies represented approximately half of those launches.

The growing complexity of ETF strategies is bringing regulatory oversight into sharper focus. On June 30, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission issued a request for public comment on ETFs seeking exposure to innovative asset classes or using novel investment strategies. The consultation examined how regulators could accommodate product innovation while maintaining investor protection and orderly markets.

The SEC raised questions around the regulatory status of certain novel ETFs, their oversight and the registration process. The public comment deadline was August 31, 2026.

The SEC has not finalized a new rule through this request. However, its review could influence how future products are structured and evaluated. For asset managers, regulatory clarity will be an important factor in determining how quickly new investment strategies can reach the market.

The ETF industry is moving beyond its traditional role as a low-cost vehicle for index investing. Active products are attracting a larger share of new capital, crypto funds are extending access to digital assets, and options-based strategies are giving investors more targeted ways to manage portfolios.

Yet traditional equity and bond funds continue to dominate industry assets. The next phase of growth will depend on whether specialized products can maintain investor demand while delivering clear investment value.

Both metals are at their lowest since September 2025. The BTC price held near $64,600, but it has fallen even harder than the metals since the hike bets took off.

Gold prices sink beneath $3,800, hitting a 14-month low as the hawkish Fed outlook and firm dollar weigh on bullion – FX

— First Squawk (@FirstSquawk) November 18, 2026

We compared the moves since November 5, the day before a strong October jobs report changed the rate outlook. Bitcoin is down 15%, silver 12.5% and gold 8.4%. Over the same days, the U.S. dollar index rose 2.2%, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed from 4.84% to 5.10%.

Higher rates hit everything that pays no interest, and gold, silver and bitcoin all fall into that group. So the next big test is the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting.

Gold peaked near $5,320 an ounce on COMEX futures in late January. It has since lost 29%, and silver has lost 60% from its January high of $115. On Monday, gold for immediate delivery touched $3,832, and Wednesday’s drop pushed it lower still.

The reason is the Fed. Markets now treat another hike as almost certain:

A quarter-point hike would lift the Fed’s target range to 4.00%-4.25%. It would be the second this year, after September’s. Waller has gone further, saying a half-point move, or “a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered.”

Central banks are still buying gold, 675 tonnes in the first nine months of the year. That hasn’t been enough to offset a stronger dollar and higher yields.

The BTC price stands at $64,590 on Binance, down 48% from its October 2025 record. On the daily chart, it sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,780, and its 200-day EMA at $75,760.

Anthropic's blockbuster debut comes as financial markets have been rocked by recent volatility, with tech stocks and crypto facing selling pressure.

The newspaper cited stronger-than-expected investor demand. Its advisers have discussed a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion.

⚠️ What if $ANT mirrors $SPCX after the IPO? pic.twitter.com/pMd9aC7KQb

— Rand Group (@randgroup) November 18, 2026

Crypto traders have been betting on the Anthropic IPO for weeks. On Hyperliquid, a pre-IPO contract that tracks one ANT share trades near $99, about 23% above $80.

We have seen this setup before. The night before SpaceX listed in June, the same kind of contract traded 28% above its $135 IPO price. SpaceX then closed its first day 19% up, below what the contract had promised.

So what should traders know before the bell rings on Thursday?

Anthropic launched its roadshow, the week when a company pitches its shares to large investors, on November 10. Its announcement set the terms:

Demand has run ahead of that. Pricing above $80 would lift the valuation toward the $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion the advisers discussed. The final price is set after the US market closes on Wednesday, and the shares open on Thursday.

Hyperliquid, a crypto exchange, lists contracts that let traders bet on a company’s share price before it lists. We compared its Anthropic contract with the one it ran for SpaceX, counting back from each listing day.

The SpaceX contract was right that the shares would jump, but too optimistic about how far. If Anthropic followed the same pattern, a 7% gap from Wednesday’s contract price would put ANT’s first close in the low $90s. That is a pattern from one listing, not a forecast.

AMD fell 8.7%, Micron dropped 10%, and Broadcom lost 6.3%, with 10 of 19 S&P 500 semiconductor stocks down at least 4%.

Nvidia declined 6.9%, extending its losing streak, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell around 4%.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 weakened as investors reassessed AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the returns from the industry's massive capital commitments.

The AI stock sell-off is widening beyond Nvidia, with semiconductor manufacturers, memory stocks and data-center suppliers facing another round of heavy selling. Micron Technology, Broadcom, AMD and Marvell were among the biggest losers on Friday, while Nvidia extended its decline.

The momentum of the selloff became more significant: 10 of the 19 S&P 500 semiconductor stocks were down at least 4%, highlighting a sector-wide repricing rather than isolated weakness. Anthropic’s record IPO has failed to restore confidence, leaving investors focused on the cost and profitability of the AI buildout.

Semiconductor stocks were among the market’s weakest performers, with losses extending across chipmakers, equipment manufacturers and AI infrastructure suppliers.

The breadth of the decline is notable. All 19 S&P 500 semiconductor stocks were trading lower in the latest market reading, while 10 had fallen at least 4%. The group was averaging a decline of approximately 5.7% among the biggest losers.

Nvidia stock fell approximately 7%, putting shares near their lowest levels since June 2025 and extending the company’s losing streak. The decline has become a broader concern for investors because Nvidia remains a key benchmark for AI spending and semiconductor demand.

AMD, Broadcom and Micron have also faced pressure, despite strong underlying demand for AI chips and memory. Investors are increasingly questioning whether elevated valuations adequately reflect the industry’s capital requirements, competition and potential returns.

The selling has also reached companies further down the AI supply chain. Marvell, Coherent, Bloom Energy, CoreWeave and Nebius have experienced significant declines, suggesting the market is reducing exposure across the broader AI infrastructure trade.

Anthropic’s public debut was expected to provide a fresh catalyst for technology stocks. Instead, the company’s shares fell sharply following their initial surge, while chip stocks continued to weaken.

ANT stock opened at $111.50, reached $115.10 and closed its first session at $97.17—17% above its $83 IPO price. However, the stock subsequently came under pressure as the broader AI sell-off intensified.

The technology sell-off has weighed heavily on broader indexes. The S&P 500 fell 1.4%, while the Nasdaq declined 2.5% in Friday trading. The Dow Jones remained comparatively resilient, reflecting its lower exposure to technology stocks.

The market is also approaching a potentially significant losing streak, with the S&P 500 on track for its seventh consecutive daily decline. The weakness follows a sharp previous-session sell-off in which the S&P 500 dropped 2%, the Nasdaq fell 2.3% and the Dow lost 2.2%.

If Nvidia and other major chipmakers stabilize, the sector could recover some of its losses. But continued weakness across semiconductor stocks would signal that investors are still reducing exposure to the AI trade.

For now, the sell-off is less about whether AI demand exists, and more about how much investors are willing to pay for that growth.

#5292. Peter Brandt Predicts More Pain for Bitcoin

Veteran commodity trader Peter Brandt has provided yet another bearish outlook for the world's largest cryptocurrency, arguing that the crypto asset could see much more misery if its historical market trends play out.

Bitcoin Bitcoin Every bull market phase in BTC's history has ended with at least a 75% correction of the previous parabolic bull trend. Could this be what's happening in Bitcoin? https://t.co/PVXJpetSyO

Brandt's latest doomsday prediction comes at a time when Bitcoin is still trying to recover from its biggest sell-off to date, which has wiped out close to half of its market value from its October 2025 peak.

The trader's latest post on X highlights a pattern he has found throughout Bitcoin's price history: previous bull runs have always ended with devastating market corrections.

"Every bull market phase in the history of BTC has ended with at least a 75% correction of the prior parabolic bull trend," Brandt's X post reads.

Continuing his warning, Brandt raised an alarming question: "Is this what is happening with Bitcoin?"

The trading veteran has not put a number on the possible crash. But his words point toward the possibility that the current drop in Bitcoin might be part of a larger correction and not just a temporary dip.

A look at Bitcoin's historical crashes could paint a scary picture.

Bitcoin has a history of sharp corrections following major bull runs.

For example, the crypto asset dropped by around 84% from its December 2017 high to its December 2018 low. Another example of such a deep price correction can be found in the 2022 bear market, when BTC saw a drop of around 77% from its November 2021 all-time high.

These historic crashes have shown the extreme losses that Bitcoin investors have faced during such market corrections.

At the time of writing on Nov. 20, Bitcoin is currently trading at around $62,000, which is almost 51% below its October 2025 all-time high.

If it were to undergo a 75% price correction from its all-time high, then it would drop to around $31,550.

But it's worth mentioning that Brandt referred to a correction of the prior parabolic bull trend, which may not be the same as a 75% correction from the peak.

Interestingly enough, this is not the first time the trader has warned about an even darker future for Bitcoin's price.

Earlier, on Nov. 15, Brandt shared a weekly BTC chart showing a potential head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern that usually signals a bearish reversal.

According to Brandt, if the pattern is confirmed, there's a chance that Bitcoin could never revisit its previous all-time high in his lifetime.

The chart he shared also indicates an important zone between $60,000 and $65,000. A confirmed breakdown below this zone could further strengthen the bearish outlook.

Moreover, there is still plenty of selling pressure in the crypto market. The latest update from Lookonchain on Nov. 19 revealed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had seen net outflows of around $975 million over the past seven days. The biggest net outflows came from BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).

BTC bounced from $62K as silver fell 14% since Nov 9. What does fund trading reveal, and is there really a shift from metals into Bitcoin?

In today’s Bitcoin news, on November 19, silver and gold are extending their sell-off, but Bitcoin is holding its ground near $63,800. BTC has bounced off the $62,000 level for the second time in four days, raising the question of whether crypto’s sell-off is finally losing steam and investors are starting to move money back into digital assets.

Silver futures closed Wednesday at $45 an ounce, down 4.8% on the day and 14% since November 9, while gold fell another 3.2%.

JUST IN: $1,400,000,000,000 wiped out from Gold and Silver in the past 24 hours. pic.twitter.com/NwLlK9b1iv

— Whale Insider (@WhaleInsider) November 19, 2026

For traders following Bitcoin news, the obvious explanation is that money is moving out of metals and into crypto. We tested that by comparing how much money changes hands each day in the three largest US funds for silver, gold, and Bitcoin. If investors were switching, Bitcoin’s slice of that trading would grow.

Well, for now it hasn’t: Bitcoin took 30% of the money traded over the past five trading days, about the same as the 31% it took over the 20 days before.

Bitcoin’s bounce also came with less trading than the sell-off before it, a sign that buyers are still cautious.

So is this the start of a shift from metals to crypto, or just a pause in the selling?

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) give a clean view of where US money goes, because they trade side by side on the same exchanges. We took the three biggest: the iShares Silver Trust (SLV), SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), and BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT). For each, we multiplied the closing price by the shares traded to get the dollars that changed hands each day.

So the money leaving silver and gold isn’t showing up in Bitcoin funds, at least not yet. It looks more like a broad sell-off in both, with metals now taking the heavier hit.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Binance’s BTCUSDT pair tells the same Bitcoin news story from the crypto side. During the drop from November 13 to 15, it traded an average of $2.0 billion a day. In the three days since, as Bitcoin held above $62,000, the average fell to $1.5 billion.

Lighter trading on a bounce means fewer buyers are stepping in. Sellers have slowed down, but buyers haven’t rushed back.

Bitcoin’s spot ETFs, which hold the coin itself, show a similar picture. IBIT took in $76.5 million on November 16, its first inflow after 11 days of outflows. That’s a start, but one day of buying after two weeks of selling.

What drives both markets is the same: the US Federal Reserve. Traders expect another rate hike in December, and higher rates hurt assets that pay no interest, from silver to Bitcoin. Until that changes, a rotation from one to the other has little to feed on.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Return After Seven-Day Losing Streak as IBIT Adds $76.5M: Is the Sell-Off Finally Over?

On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $63,713. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,245, and its 200-day EMA at $75,624.

The Bitcoin news to watch is volume. A move above $65,500 with trading back near $2 billion a day would be a start. If IBIT’s share of fund trading also climbs above a third, money is actually moving from metals to crypto.

#5289. Worse Than 2008? Peter Schiff Issues Terrifying Market Crash Warning

Noted economist and longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has sounded the alarm about an upcoming financial apocalypse, warning that the crisis could be worse than the historic 2008 market crash.

On Nov. 20, Peter Schiff shared a series of troubling X posts warning about the potential for significant losses in the U.S. stock market, real estate, and cryptocurrencies amid escalating financial system stress.

The economist shared a video with a very alarming headline: "The Next Crash Will Be Worse Than 2008."

In one of his most recent posts on X, Schiff argued that the recent gold price downtrend might signal a grim outlook for other key asset classes.

"It's probably a bad sign that gold is falling this much. It probably means that the stock and real estate markets are going to fall even more in percentage terms," Schiff cautioned.

According to Peter Schiff, gold's recent price behavior could be signaling deflation. As a result, this might lead to a more severe financial crisis.

However, Peter Schiff is convinced that the Federal Reserve will step in to prevent this financial apocalypse.

"Gold is signaling deflation. But asset deflation would bust the government and the banking system, so the Fed will pivot to avoid it," the economist explained.

Simply put, Schiff assumes that the Federal Reserve will pivot and introduce monetary stimulus to prevent a financial meltdown.

In another startling prediction, the economist warned that the U.S. stock market might wipe out all its gains since President Donald Trump took office.

"There's a good chance that the U.S. stock market is about to give back all the gains since Trump took office," the economist predicted.

He also warned that there might be a recession. As a result, Trump will likely point to Democrats and their wins in the recent midterm elections as the reason for this recession.

Interestingly enough, Peter Schiff's bearish outlook also applies to Bitcoin (BTC), which has already suffered significant losses amid the overall market crash.

On Nov. 18, Peter Schiff shared several alarming market indicators. According to his data, the Nasdaq has dropped 12.25%. AI infrastructure company CoreWeave has plummeted 64%.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has plunged 33.5% from its 2026 peak.

Additionally, the economist noted that the U.S. housing market index had dropped to 25, its lowest level since 2012. This shows that the economic issues go well beyond AI stocks.

"Still think this is just about AI?" he asked.

On the 19th of November, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said in an interview with CNBC that the recent crypto market sell-off is a result of capital rotating into IPOs like Anthropic. However, he does expect the markets to rebound once the listing is complete.

Still on-chain data for XRP suggests that despite on-chain indicators looking bullish, the altcoin is struggling to move beyond the $1 psychological level.

Garlinghouse argued that the recent bloodbath across digital assets is less about a fundamental collapse in crypto and more about investors shifting funds to chase the AI boom.

He pointed to a previous sell-off in the market, acknowledging,

We also saw a sell-off very similar when SpaceX went public. What happens is… people are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market in crypto, including Bitcoin and XRP, and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Athropic IPO… What we saw after the SpaceX IPO is a rally in the crypto market.

He believes that the same story will play out with the Anthropic IPO too.

Garlinghouse’s bullish thesis does have a solid footing. Most notably, CryptoQuant’s data shows that the XRP Exchange Reserve on Binance has been declining over the last thirty days.

In late October 2026, Binance held roughly 2.7 billion XRP, but the figure dropped to 2.47 billion XRP as of the 19th of November.

When Exchange Reserve falls, it typically signals that investors are moving coins to self-custody, reducing the immediate supply available for selling.

Despite the tightening supply on exchanges, XRP’s price action remains volatile. At press time, XRP was trading at $0.9834, down 1.4% in the last 24 hours.

The chart further revealed a market struggling to find firm footing. XRP managed to hold above $1 during November 12-14 before a steep drop dragged it down to the $0.90 region.

The last 24 hours saw the asset sail briefly above $1 but faced an immediate rejection, slumping back into the high $0.90s.

As XRP remains in a tug-of-war between falling exchange reserves and repeated price rejections at $1.00, investors are uncertain about its next direction.

If Garlinghouse is correct and digital assets do rally after the Anthropic IPO, the rotation will easily cause prices to soar beyond $1. However, until that macroeconomic shift occurs, XRP holders appear content to move their coins off exchanges and wait out the storm.

Several key moving averages continue to cluster in the $75,000 - $76,000 region, adding resistance for Bitcoin price action.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

Both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these new plans.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”

The registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

However, an important distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being launched in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

These numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

This, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

XRP may have room to recover toward $1.06 and $1.07, according to the host of Cilinix Crypto, whose latest XRP analysis points to tentative signs of a bottom. The forecast is conditional: renewed weakness in equities could instead send the token back toward $0.90 and $0.85.

#5284. Italian Banking Giant Rotates Crypto ETF Portfolio From Bitcoin to Solana and XRP

Italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a new disclosure. This follows capital rotation out of Bitcoin products by a slew of traditional firms amid dwindling market sentiment.

The bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways. In June, total assets were worth $90 million as it looked to diversify and grow holdings systematically.

Bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets. At the end of Q2, BTC holdings stood at $69.32 million but dropped slightly to above $61 million last quarter. The firm’s Ethereum exposure also dropped to $5 million.

However, Solana and XRP products filled the vacuum, highlighting institutional appetite for these assets. At the time of writing, the bank’s spot Solana ETF exposure is at $14.1 million after its investment in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF ballooned from seven shares to 875,407 shares.

Intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The company’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

More broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

Historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

The former have the potential to record spikes within the red wave, like in 2022 before the approval of spot ETF products in the United States. These products opened up digital assets to a new stash of traditional capital.

Intesa and other banks have since increased their crypto exposure, driven by the need to diversify assets and a broader adoption spree. Heightened institutional and retail interests pushed Bitcoin to an all-time high above $125k last year. Currently, BTC trades at $63,819, while Ethereum is slightly below $1,800.

"Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

Kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally."

The author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

"With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

In late August, Kiyosaki said on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he said.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

#5282. Eight Years: From a Crypto Exchange to a Global Ecosystem Serving 40 Million Users

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

In 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each company can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

WhiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The company also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into new products and services.

“Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making new technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” said Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

DacityCoin started as a background joke. In Rockstar’s launch trailer, the name is painted on a stunt plane. Then this week, gameplay footage from Brazilian streamer Combo Infinito showed an in-game phone app listing “DacityCoin (DCTY)”, complete with buy and sell buttons.

Crypto traders did what crypto traders do: within hours, the Solana token with the same ticker went vertical.

Before the footage, DCTY had never been worth more than about $54,000. Here’s what its main pool on DEX Screener shows now:

One important detail: Rockstar hasn’t linked the in-game coin to any real token, and DCTY has no official tie to GTA 6 or Take-Two. The name game is getting messy, too.

A separate Pump.fun token called “Dacity Coin” hit a $10.8 million market value on Wednesday, then slid to about $800,000. Exchange Bitrue joined in as well, listing DacityCoin futures with up to 10x leverage on Wednesday.

If a fresh meme coin season were kicking off, Pump.fun is where you’d see it first, since that’s where most new Solana tokens of this kind are born. So we pulled PumpSwap’s daily trading from DefiLlama, which tracks exchange data across blockchains.

Outside the GTA hype, the bigger meme coins are having a rough year. All eight large meme coins we tracked on Binance are down for 2026, by a median of 54%, while Bitcoin is down 28%. The past week stung too, with drops between 11% and 23%:

Source: Binance daily closes, Coinspeaker calculation, November 19.

Zoom out, and DCTY is still tiny. The whole meme coin sector is worth $22.5 billion on CoinGecko, with Solana’s share at only $2 billion. One token can steal the spotlight for a day, but a real run for meme coins needs the big names and overall trading to rise together. So far, that hasn’t happened.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Top Solana Meme Coins to Bid

Pump.fun did get a payday out of the DacityCoin rush. The platform earned $1.62 million in revenue on Wednesday, up from a $1.28 million average over the five days before. Since April, Pump.fun says it spends half its revenue buying PUMP on the open market, so a day like Wednesday means roughly $800,000 of buying.

The worst day was November 14, when PUMP dropped 15%. Token trackers list a scheduled release of locked PUMP tokens in mid-November, though they don’t agree on the exact date. So far, buybacks of under $1 million a day haven’t been enough to soak up that selling.

GTA 6 meme coins are hot now, but the thing to watch is breadth, meaning how many coins move together. If PumpSwap volume stays above $300 million a day after launch week and Dogecoin or Pepe join in, DacityCoin could be the start of something bigger.

If DCTY fades and volume slips back to $150 million, it’ll go down as a fun launch-day story and not much more.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

On 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

#5277. XRP Ledger Breaks Vote Stall on Bank-Style Lending: What It Unlocks for XRP Holders

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain."

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool showed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed."

#5272. Binance Hack-Linked Wallet Moves 34,279 ETH, but Investigators See No Confirmed Sale

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of inactivity. The ether was worth roughly $63 million at prices used in Tuesday’s reporting. That is a significant movement of suspected stolen funds, but a wallet transfer is not automatically a sale, a successful laundering step or proof that the recipient controls are independent of the sender. Investigators had not identified the new addresses as exchanges at the time of their initial reports.

Monitoring groups MistTrack and Solid Intel reported the transfers on November 17. MistTrack described three movements of approximately 12,000 ETH, 12,000 ETH and 10,279.66 ETH. The receiving wallets were newly created, and the monitored funds had not moved again when the analysts published their findings. Public transaction records make it possible to trace the amounts and destinations, but they do not disclose the human operator behind each address. The link to the earlier breach rests on investigators’ attribution of the sending wallet, not a label embedded in the blockchain itself.

The October attack involved vastly larger losses than Tuesday’s movement. US investigators attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking group, and authorities have announced substantial asset restraints and seizures. Blockchain intelligence firms have also tracked funds moved through different assets and protocols. These parallel developments should not be added together casually, because frozen, seized, recovered and still-controlled amounts describe different legal and operational states. The fresh ETH transfers are one piece of a complex post-incident trail rather than an update to the full net-loss number.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's custody and security precautions.

Crypto trading commentary sometimes treats any transfer from an exploit-linked wallet as preparation to dump tokens. That can happen, but the evidence here does not yet establish a market sale. Transfers may consolidate funds, redistribute control or precede another operation. Until an address is linked to a trading venue, bridge, mixer or other service, the immediate observable fact is the destination change. Even a later exchange deposit would need careful interpretation: deposits are not identical to executed sell orders. Reporting should preserve those steps rather than collapsing them into one dramatic conclusion.

Ethereum’s public ledger lets investigators monitor known addresses and alert service providers if assets reappear at identifiable points. Token issuers, exchanges and law enforcement may each have different powers depending on the assets and jurisdictions involved. Native ETH cannot simply be frozen by an issuer in the way some centrally administered tokens can. That difference complicates recovery when funds leave services that can intervene. The next useful evidence will be further movements, identification of services receiving the funds and official updates to the case.

Investigators can improve attribution confidence by comparing the sequence, amounts and transaction timing with addresses already associated with the incident. Yet public labels can be incomplete, and a newly created wallet may simply be another address controlled by the same actor. Readers should resist claims that funds have reached a criminal group, a particular country or a cash-out desk unless that identification is supported by additional evidence. Future investigative notices should specify their degree of confidence and distinguish observed transfers from hypotheses about their purpose.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet compromise.

The latest transfer warrants close monitoring, but it should not be reported as the disposal of $63 million in stolen ether without further proof. The distinction between observable transactions and inferred intent is especially important in a security incident of this scale.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk report of MistTrack and Solid Intel monitoring · MistTrack transfer report

#5270. Bitcoin’s $700M liquidation wave deepens – Is crypto’s $2T market cap at risk?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Anthropic’s post-IPO performance appears to have created a volatile market setup.

On the technical side, ANT opened at $111.50, around 34% above its $83 IPO price, before losing much of its early gains and closing at $97.17. This shows that initial demand was strong, but profit-taking quickly kicked in. The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

Naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility? Interestingly, recent Glassnode data points to a possible link. As the chart below shows, Anthropic futures on crypto platforms recorded $9.5 billion in trading volume ahead of its Nasdaq debut. In comparison, SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, attracted $3.9 billion in pre-listing futures volume before its June debut.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

This highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a new record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype quickly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

So, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

According to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

Worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

So, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

ANT’s IPO may have added to Bitcoin’s fear and increased crypto selling.

Weak liquidity could keep pressure on crypto, putting the $2 trillion market cap at risk.

#5269. US Senators Question SEC Tokenized-Stock Exemption Over Wallet Transfers and Investor Protection

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors and prevent illicit transfers. Their November 16 letter, reported by The Block, takes aim at gaps they see in the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for certain trading venues. The development is an oversight challenge, not a court ruling or a notice that the exemption has been cancelled. It goes to a central difficulty for tokenized securities: a regulated purchase can become a blockchain transfer to another address.

The SEC introduced its approach in September, allowing qualifying tokenized-securities venues to operate under a defined exemption from some ordinary exchange-registration requirements. The aim is to permit experimentation with trading stocks in token form while the agency assesses a new market structure. A token representing a security still raises questions about ownership, trading rules and investor rights. The exemptions and their precise conditions matter more than a general statement that securities have moved on-chain. Not every blockchain token, broker or venue automatically qualifies for the same regulatory treatment.

Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto reportedly told SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the framework lacks sufficiently specific safeguards around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering procedures. A buyer verified by a regulated venue might later transfer a token to a wallet whose controller has not undergone the same checks. This problem is not solved merely by verifying the identity of the first purchaser. The letter asks how secondary transfers and the reach of compliance obligations would be managed once tokens circulate beyond the initial venue.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's developing licensing rules.

The senators raised concerns about retail-investor protections and pricing, and reportedly asked whether companies could opt out of having their shares tokenized. Those questions are distinct from financial-crime screening. A token that references equity needs a clear relationship to the rights and obligations of the underlying security, as well as fair information about execution and ownership. If an issuer’s wishes, the investor’s expectations and the platform’s legal structure do not line up, technical transferability alone cannot resolve the conflict. Policymakers must address those issues in enforceable terms.

The lawmakers asked the SEC to explain its approach and urged a transparent rulemaking process for changes in the regulatory treatment of tokenized securities. Such a letter can affect oversight and public debate, especially as control of congressional committees changes, but it is not itself binding legislation. Venues exploring tokenized equities should continue to follow the actual exemption terms and any subsequent SEC guidance. The next concrete milestones are the agency’s response, proposed revisions if any, and how early trading models implement identity, custody and transfer restrictions.

For related context, see our earlier report on new institutional crypto-custody arrangements.

Tokenization can change how securities move, but it does not automatically settle which rules should accompany them. The dispute now concerns the design of that regulatory perimeter, with no basis to describe the senators’ letter as an immediate prohibition on tokenized stocks.

Reporting sources: The Block report of four senators’ letter

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG company that builds on Bittensor.

At Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert said that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence."

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson said.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

The November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

#5267. Uhm, Netflix, What Is This? CZ Slams The Altruists for Making Him the Villain Behind FTX’s Collapse

The Altruists by Netflix makes CZ the villain of FTX’s fall. Our FTT data shows the crash came after FTX asked Binance for help.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, known as CZ, has hit back at The Altruists Netflix series about the fall of FTX, which premiered on November 19. The show has found a villain for the story, and it is not the man serving 25 years in prison for it.

The Altruists Netflix release is a scripted drama, not a documentary, which may explain a few things. Its eight episodes follow Sam Bankman-Fried, played by Anthony Boyle, and his former girlfriend Caroline Ellison. Terry Chen plays CZ, cast as the rival who brought Bankman-Fried down.

There are forces spreading negative narratives, with massive amounts of funding behind it. https://t.co/Ymy4sA0cJd

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) November 20, 2026

The real story is hardly a mystery. A US jury convicted Bankman-Fried of fraud after a month-long trial, and a judge sentenced him to 25 years in prison. Three years on, Netflix has somehow reopened the question of who is to blame. So did CZ and Binance really sink FTX, as the show suggests?

We went back to the token prices from the week FTX fell to check.

The series, co-created by Graham Moore and Jacqueline Hoyt, is built around Bankman-Fried’s relationship with Ellison, who ran Alameda Research, FTX’s sister trading firm. Netflix’s own page for the show sums it up in one line: “Young, idealistic and suddenly worth billions, they tried to do good—but unleashed the worst in each other.”

Zhao is a supporting character, but a central one in the plot. The show has him setting a trap that pushes Bankman-Fried into front-running, which means trading ahead of customers’ orders to profit from them. Some viewers also read it as pressure on FTX to hand over trading data.

Critics have attacked the show on other points too. Constance Wang, FTX’s former chief operating officer, who is a character in the series, criticized its inaccuracies and its framing as a love story. Other critics say the focus on the couple’s romance downplays Bankman-Fried’s own responsibility for the fraud.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Binance Listings

CZ did not write a long rebuttal. On the morning of November 20, he shared a Forbes commentary on X. The piece said The Altruists Netflix storyline turns him into a “crypto villain” and invents the front-running trap, and that there is no public evidence Zhao ever did such a thing.

He also posted a comparison image from March. In his words, it “already said it all.” Later that day he went further, saying that forces backed by huge financial support are spreading negative stories about him. He did not say who.

Yi He, Binance’s co-founder, was blunter. In a post in Chinese, she called the show’s characters thin and clichéd. “If you’re the protagonist, even your crimes are someone else’s fault,” she wrote. She compared it unfavourably with Hongguo, a Chinese short-drama app, and added: “Netflix might as well cancel it outright.”

Netflix and the showrunners have not responded publicly.

EXPLORE: BNB Crypto Drops 8.7% in an Hour as Binance Loses $6.36 Billion to Hackers, and Futures Traders Turn Short: Can BNB Hold Its 200-Day Average?

The real Binance did play a part in the final week. Here is the order of events in November 2022:

To see which of these moments broke FTX, we tracked FTT’s hourly price on Binance through that week.

Zhao’s post alone did not sink the token. FTT traded at $24.34 in the hour he posted it. Thirty-three hours later, at midnight UTC on November 8, it was still at $22.08, only 9% lower. Ellison had publicly offered to buy Binance’s FTT at $22, and the price held close to that.

The real crash came on November 8. FTT closed the hour of the deal announcement at $17.93, then hit $2.51 three hours later, a fall of 86%. That is when a run became a collapse: the rescue deal told the market that FTX could not pay its customers on its own.

Today FTT trades at about $0.17, down 99.3% from the hour of Zhao’s post.

A run like this only kills an exchange that does not hold its customers’ money. FTX did not. About $8 billion in customer deposits was missing, used to cover Alameda’s trading losses and spending.

At the 2023 trial, Ellison testified that Alameda had been taking FTX customer money for years, on Bankman-Fried’s instructions. The jury convicted him on all seven counts. The US Attorney’s Office in Manhattan announced in March 2024 that he had been sentenced to 25 years and ordered to forfeit about $11 billion. Ellison received two years.

Zhao has a criminal record of his own, from a separate case. He pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to run an effective anti-money-laundering program at Binance and served four months in prison. Binance agreed to pay more than $4 billion, and President Trump pardoned him in October 2025.

Sam Bankman-Fried may be the UNLUCKIEST investor in history.

If FTX hadn’t SOLD its investments after the collapse, it would still hold:

Anthropic: $34.7 billion (69x)Robinhood: $4.3 billion (7x)Solana: $2.9 billion (1.1x)Cursor: $1.8 billion (9,000x)Sui: $600 million (6x)… pic.twitter.com/GdHj3Lldaw

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) November 16, 2026

The FTX estate has also gone after Binance. In November 2024 it sued Binance and Zhao for about $1.76 billion, saying the 2021 buyback of Binance’s FTX stake was paid with customer money. It also claimed his November 2022 posts helped set off the run. Binance has called the claims meritless.

So The Altruists Netflix version is right that Zhao’s post lit the fuse. It leaves out that the hole was there long before he posted, and FTT’s price only collapsed once FTX had to ask for a rescue.

Geneva, Switzerland –  TRON DAO, the community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet through blockchain technology and decentralized applications (dApps), today announced that the Aave App, a high-yield savings mobile app developed and managed by Aave Labs, will add support for USDT (TRC-20) deposits on the TRON network as it expands to Android following its initial launch on iOS.

The launch combines Android’s global reach with TRON’s leading role in the stablecoin ecosystem, expanding mobile access to onchain savings opportunities that are not accessible on traditional savings apps. With support for USDT on TRON, eligible users in supported jurisdictions can now deposit USDT on TRON and start earning yield on their savings.

Android’s extensive global footprint offers a significant distribution opportunity for digital asset applications, particularly in markets where stablecoins are used for payments, remittances, and savings. TRON provides an established infrastructure for this opportunity, with more than $94 billion in circulating USDT, the largest circulating supply of Tether’s dollar-pegged stablecoin among blockchain networks. TRON also supports a broad range of stablecoin use cases, including payments, cross-border transfers, and digital asset transactions.

Aave is building the World’s Savings App, a simple, globally accessible tool designed to help people grow and manage their savings, with a delightful design experience on the surface and powerful onchain finance infrastructure working under the hood. Users of the app can earn yield on their savings, enjoy flexible access to their funds, and benefit from the Balance Protection program. They can also deposit and withdraw via stablecoins or banks in eligible countries and project their potential savings growth over the years with a future simulator. Following its availability on iOS, the Android launch expands the app’s mobile reach, while TRON support connects users to one of the largest USDT ecosystems in onchain finance.

“Aave Labs has a proven track record of building leading DeFi products, and the Aave App brings that expertise to everyday users,” said Justin Sun, Founder of TRON. “With TRON support on Android and iOS, more people can use the USDT they already hold on TRON to access simple, accessible onchain savings with the Aave App.”

“Millions of people in emerging economies already rely on stablecoins on TRON to save and send money,” said Stani Kulechov, Founder and CEO of Aave Labs. “The Aave App lets them earn on those dollars.”

By enabling USDT deposits through the Aave App on Android, the integration connects TRON’s established stablecoin ecosystem with a consumer-focused mobile application. The launch reflects the continued convergence of mobile applications and blockchain infrastructure, as consumer-focused products work to make digital assets and decentralized financial services more accessible worldwide.

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of November 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 414 million in total user accounts, more than 16 billion in total transactions, and over $24 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”

#5265. Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

This drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

On Thursday, November 19, AI company Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

With the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

CoinGlass data shows $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

According to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is currently trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

Bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

Zcash leveraged bullish positions have come under pressure in the last 24 hours, with reported data showing a 1,483% liquidation imbalance in favor of long-position wipeouts.

According to CoinGlass data, Zcash recorded more than $14 million ($14.07 million) in liquidations over 24 hours, with nearly 93% coming from long positions. Liquidated longs were $13.16 million against shorts of $917,620, a difference of 1,483%.

Long traders have taken most of the forced closures in this market, with Zcash being hit hard by the ongoing market sell-off. Significant long liquidations were seen for Zcash, accelerating its price decline as leveraged positions unwind, particularly with traders being heavily concentrated on the same side of the market.

At the time of writing, ZEC was down 14.53% in the last 24 hours, recording the heaviest losses in the top 20, while NEAR Protocol was down 13.03% in the same timeframe.

Zcash is currently testing support at the 200-day MA ($809); a further drop would target $775 and then $700. A short-term price recovery for Zcash would see it aim for a return to four figures, eyeing the 50-day MA at $1,164.

Zcash is entering its third day of a drop that began on November 18, even as the broader crypto market slid as the tech-stock selloff spread. The rapid unwind suggests a leverage shakeout amid volatility following Anthropic’s IPO.

Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, under the ticker symbol ANT, raising about $81.3 billion in the public offering (and $107.3 billion combined with a $26 billion private placement).

Over the last 24 hours, volume across crypto futures rose 29.31% to $250 billion, while open interest (OI) fell 3.07% to $109.29 billion, according to CoinGlass data. That combination suggests traders are unwinding positions, with net capital exiting the futures market.

Liquidations across the crypto market increased by 88.66% to $773.76 million, and longs accounted for 87.2% of the total, meaning leveraged bets on higher prices were forced shut as prices fell.
